chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Mu'ttab, who said:
Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) used to order us, whenever the fruit became ripe/harvested, to take it out and sell it, and buy [new fruit] with the Muslims, on a day-to-day basis.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended method for selling and buying fruit according to Imam Al-Reza (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated from Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him), outlines a specific commercial strategy for handling fresh produce to avoid the complexities of *gharar* (uncertainty) and *rib al-nasi'ah* (interest-based delay) inherent in selling perishable goods on credit. By selling the harvest immediately for cash and repurchasing it on a 'day-for-day' basis, believers ensure liquidity and freshness while maintaining a continuous supply, a practice highly regarded in Shia jurisprudence for its practical wisdom in market transactions.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Mohsan Bin Ahmad, from Yunus Bin yaqoub, from Mo’tab who said,
‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> used to order us whenever we realised the fruit harvest that we should take it out and sell them, and buy along with the Muslims, on a day to day basis’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah, from Muhsin ibn Ahmad from Yunus ibn Ya’qub from Mu‘attib who has said the following:
“Abu al-Hassan ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would command, at the time of harvest of fruit, to take them out and sell and then buy every day as Muslim people do.”
